MGIMS Pays Tribute to Badi Behenji on Her 25th Death Anniversary
Monday, 05 January 2026
1293 Hits
Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (MGIMS), Sevagram solemnly observed the 25th death anniversary of its revered founder-director, Dr. Sushila Nayar, fondly remembered as
Badi Behenji
. The occasion was marked by reverence, reflection, and a reaffirmation of the values she lived by and imparted to generations.
Dr AK Shukla (Dean,MGIMS), Dr. Poonam Shivkumar Varma (Medical Superintendent, Kasturba Hospital) along with faculty members, staff, and students, paid floral tributes by garlanding her portrait at
Maatru-Sthal
. Several admirers expressed their homage by bowing with folded hands and performing
parikrama
around her memorial.
An inclusive, all-religion prayer was organised to mark the occasion, reflecting Dr. Nayar’s belief in universal harmony and spiritual inclusiveness. The gathering recited the concluding verses of the second chapter of the
Bhagavad Gita
and rendered hymns from the
Upanishads
,
Quran
,
Japji Sahib
, and
Bible
, symbolising unity beyond religious boundaries.
A recorded message of Dr. Sushila Nayar was played on the occasion, deeply moving the audience. In her discourse, she spoke of the timeless truth that
“Tu Vishuposhak hai”
—that every individual is a nurturer of life and society. She emphasised that the path towards the
Paramatma
lies in collective upliftment, not in isolation. True spiritual progress, she reminded, is achieved by taking people along, by serving selflessly, and by walking together towards compassion and understanding. She explained that when one lives a life rooted in service and empathy, the distinction between
atma
and
paramatma
dissolves, leading to their ultimate union.
Dr. Sushila Nayar, who led MGIMS from 1969 to 2000, profoundly shaped the institution’s moral and spiritual ethos. During Friday evening prayers, she used to impart life lessons centred on truth, humility, compassion, and social responsibility—teachings that continue to resonate within the MGIMS community.
To commemorate her memory through service, the Department of Pathology organised its annual blood donation camp. The camp was inaugurated by Dr A K Shukla (Dean MGIMS),  and Dr Poonam Verma Shivkumar (Medical Superintendent, Kasturba Hospital), who lit the ceremonial lamp and garlanded the portraits of Ba, Bapu, and Badi Behenji. Dr. Anupama Gupta (Head of the Department of Pathology) along with faculty members and students, actively participated in the camp. A total of 30 voluntary donors donated 350 ml of blood each after completing the requisite health checks.

During Friday evening prayers, she used to impart life lessons centred on truth, humility, compassion, and social responsibility—teachings that continue to resonate within the MGIMS community.

Dr. Anupama Gupta (Head of the Department of Pathology) along with faculty members and students, actively participated in the camp. A total of 30 voluntary donors donated 350 ml of blood each after completing the requisite health checks.
